title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The elimination from (62) to (63) is correct only under conventions not stated on the page: ε_0^2 = ℓ_0 (ε_i a square root of ℓ_i, the order-2 orbifold loop) and σ_∞(ε_0) = ε_1. Under these, σ_∞(ε_0)^r ξ^{-1} ℓ_0^γ ε_0^{-r} = ε_1^r ξ^{-1} ε_0^{γ+β}, as written. Presumably these conventions are fixed earlier in the notes.

The 'donc' giving the two forms ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} or λℓ_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1} is asserted without proof. Checking that these forms satisfy the 3-cycle relation is easy: it uses ρ^3 = 1, ρ(ℓ_0) = ℓ_1, ρ(ℓ_1) = ℓ_∞ and ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1. The converse, that every profinite solution has one of these forms, is a nontrivial statement about torsion and conjugacy of finite subgroups in profinite completions of virtually free groups (cf. later work of Herfort–Zalesskii type). It is a gap, not an error.
The last line, describing how ξ' is expressed in terms of λ', breaks off unfinished.

ideas.what: Encoding automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} compatible with the S_3 × Z/2 action by a 3-cycle relation, a twisted 2-cycle relation and a unit condition 2γ+1 ∈ Ẑ*.
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations (I), (II), (III) of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT
ideas.where_published: Only programmatic hints in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; not these explicit equations.

ideas.what: Solving ξρ(ξ)ρ^2(ξ) = 1 as ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} or λℓ_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1}, i.e. via non-abelian H^1(Z/3, π̂) and the two conjugacy classes of order-3 elements.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological interpretation of the GT relations; conjugacy classes of torsion in (π̂ ⋊ Z/3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, 'A cohomological interpretation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group' (Invent. Math. 1997)

ideas.what: Working in Ŝ^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^ and reducing to SL(2,Z/6) to test congruence conditions on the 'cyclotomic' parameter p.
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT-type automorphisms on profinite SL_2(Z)/PSL_2(Z); congruence quotients
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in La Longue Marche (1981).

ideas.what: Elimination of the auxiliary variable g_0 and change of variables r = γ−β, s = γ+β.

missed.claim: Grothendieck, years before Lochak–Schneps (1997), solves the 3-cycle relation by a non-abelian coboundary/cocycle description. The two classes correspond to the two order-3 fixed points of ρ. This is essentially the cohomological interpretation of GT relation (II), here intertwined with the PGL_2(Z) orbifold picture.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority and history point for the GT literature. It also shows that Grothendieck parametrized GT-type elements via torsion lifts in PGL_2(Ẑ), a viewpoint later rediscovered.

missed.claim: The promised explicit identification of σ_∞ and f in SL(2,Ẑ), to test the mod-3 condition on p, is deferred here; the follow-up only starts on the next page.
missed.quote: il faut pouvoir identifier σ_∞ et f comme éléments de Sl(2,Ẑ) - explicitation que nous ferons tantôt
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether congruence conditions on λ (here p mod 3) are forced by GT relations is studied in the modern literature. Grothendieck's computation could be compared with known results on the image of ĜT.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an unpublished, pre-Drinfeld derivation of GT-type relations, including a cohomological solution of the 3-cycle relation that anticipates Lochak–Schneps. However, Grothendieck's anticipation of GT is broadly known, and the computations are partly convention-dependent and fragmentary.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: σ_∞ and f appear separated by a comma with a small insertion, plausibly 'et', written above.
In (62) the third line begins with a struck-out symbol before g_0; the remaining equation reads g_0 = φ̂(ξ) ε_0^{γ−β}.
Under 'r+s+1' in (63) the underbrace label is 'p'.
Last lines: 'Ici ξ est déterminé mod transformation ξ' = ℓ_0^α ξ ℓ_1^{-α} ou λ' = ℓ_0^α λ dans ξ' devient…'; a struck-out symbol precedes ℓ_0^α.
